children: Technology stocks have fallen for three sessions, Asia is tumbling and inflation fears are back.
September starts with a tech selloff
Nasdaq
futures slipped roughly 0.2% Wednesday after the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1% during Tuesday’s session.
The S&P 500 lost 0.7%, while the Dow fell 419 points, or 0.8%. All three indexes have now declined for three consecutive trading days.
Nvidia fell 1.5%, AMD dropped 2.4% and Amazon
as investors reduced exposure to expensive growth stocks.
Treasury yields in the spotlight
Nasdaq market breadth was notably weak, with 128 stocks reaching new 52-week lows against only 19 new highs. September has arrived with its historical reputation intact.
The US ten-year Treasury yield climbed above 4.81%, its highest since November 2023. Higher yields increase borrowing costs and make bonds more competitive with stocks.
They also reduce the present value of future earnings — particularly inconvenient when much of your valuation lives several optimistic years from now.
Oil turns into a rate-hike catalyst
Brent crude surged more than $4 Tuesday and approached $96 Wednesday, while WTI crossed $91.

Fresh US strikes on Iranian positions prompted missile and drone retaliation against American bases, while attacks on commercial tankers deepened concerns over the effectively closed Strait of Hormuz.

Oil has gained roughly 8% in two sessions, reviving inflation fears precisely as the Fed considers another rate increase. Markets now price around a 67% probability of a quarter-point September hike, up from approximately 40% one week ago.

Asia absorbed the next wave of selling. South Korea’s chip-heavy Kospi plunged more than 3%, Japan’s Nikkei dropped 2.6% and the broader Asia-Pacific index lost 1.5%. Japanese five-year yields reached a record 2.295%, spreading the valuation pressure well beyond Wall Street.
AI delivers one piece of good news
Dell jumped around 7% after hours after record quarterly revenue of $47 billion and adjusted earnings of $7.04 per share beat expectations.
Management raised annual revenue guidance to $192 billion, up by $25 billion, while AI-server bookings exceeded $130 billion over the past year. Infrastructure demand clearly remains awake.
Broadcom reports Wednesday after the closing bell, with revenue expected near $29.2 billion and adjusted earnings around $3.23 per share.
ADP employment data provides Wednesday’s macro test before Friday’s payroll report. The dollar index rose toward 99.8, gold slid below its 200-day moving average and Bitcoin weakened modestly.

title: IXIC: Nasdaq Futures Slip After Surging Oil Sends Treasury Yields Above 4.8%
